old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a cluster of daisies in full bloom, their white petals and vibrant yellow centers standing out vividly against a backdrop of lush green foliage. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing closely on the flowers to highlight their intricate details. The sunlight bathes the scene, casting soft shadows and enhancing the natural beauty of the daisies. The gentle breeze causes some of the petals to sway slightly, adding a dynamic element to the otherwise tranquil setting. The background is softly blurred, ensuring that the viewer's attention remains fixed on the delicate flowers. There are no animals or characters present; the focus is solely on the natural beauty of the daisies and their surroundings. The overall atmosphere is peaceful and inviting, evoking a sense of calm and appreciation for nature's simple yet stunning creations.

caption: The video captures a close-up garden view of several white daisies with bright yellow central disks, lit by strong daylight. A sharply focused bloom sits at the center, another rides a tall stem at the upper right, and a third angles in from the lower left, while blurred daisies and green foliage fill the background. A small patch of pink edges the bottom-right corner. Throughout the excerpt the flower heads sway gently and continuously, the central daisy tilting and rotating slightly as its white petals rock and shift the shadow patterns across their surfaces. The tall upper-right flower leans a little on its stem, and the lower-left daisy's petals turn subtly in orientation. The blurred background blossoms stay largely fixed while the in-focus flowers drift against them. The camera stays essentially steady while the plants themselves keep moving, the swaying already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

draft_caption: The video captures a close-up garden view of several white daisies with bright yellow central disks, lit by strong daylight. A sharply focused bloom sits at the center, another rides a tall stem at the upper right, and a third angles in from the lower left, while blurred daisies and green foliage fill the background. A small patch of pink edges the bottom-right corner. Throughout the excerpt the flower heads sway gently and continuously, the central daisy tilting and rotating slightly as its white petals rock and shift the shadow patterns across their surfaces. The tall upper-right flower leans a little on its stem, and the lower-left daisy's petals turn subtly in orientation. The out-of-focus background blossoms move slightly relative to the in-focus flowers, confirming small object motion rather than a fixed scene. The camera holds still while the plants themselves keep moving, the swaying already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.
